title: Experiment on a copy
hook: A duplicate makes the original state available beside an edited version.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that editing a duplicate keeps the original untouched, so you can compare or go back after experimenting

misconception: If an edit goes wrong, you can always get the original back.
objective: Distinguish original and duplicate in a local experiment.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: A duplicate makes the original state available beside an edited version. Which preserves a separate original here? Correct option: Edit a duplicate. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The copy has its own visible identifier. The second operation edits it while preserving the original file; a duplicate in one location is not a resilient backup.

recall.question: You want to try a risky reformat of a spreadsheet but may want the old version back. What do you do first?
options: Duplicate it and edit the copy
Rename it, then edit the file
Edit it, then press Save at once
recall.why: A duplicate keeps the original beside the edited version; renaming or saving still changes the one file.
